report:
Reviewed the complete meta.book.sage_chapters claim and both associated tests. The sole implementation entry remains the explicit TODO region in spec_plan.rs; this approval accepts its documented deferral, not complete implementation.

Source assessment: generates_crate_and_module_chapters_for_both_mdbook_protocols uses a real subprocess preprocessor fixture with configured manual/src and three .sage files under design/crates. For both items/sections protocols it asserts the exact chapter set, unchanged handwritten content, crate/module numbering and parents, nested module count, source-derived HTML paths, iframe/full-page relative explorer links, purpose and dependency prose, declaration prose, generated asset existence, and absence of handwritten Markdown copies. Captured Fixture and chapters helpers establish actual file creation and preprocessing, and recursively reject duplicate source paths. Captured book.rs generates one inventory entry per model namespace, nests modules under crate overviews, prints purpose/dependencies/modules in document_outline, and writes the shared browser asset beside book sources. This supports chapter hierarchy, overview contents, configured source location, source identity and no manual Markdown-copy aspects. Static iframe/asset generation supports the intended offline delivery structure; asset existence alone does not establish all browser interactions or runtime offline operation.

The second test, todo::sage_sources_render_as_book_chapters, intentionally contains no assertions. Its matching TODO implementation explanation explicitly defers rendering with shared search, declaration links and Rust context independently of Crates insertion. The prerequisite for replacing it is complete shared architecture-browser delivery and substantive integration/browser assertions for those interactions, including server-independent built-book operation and shared inventory behavior. Those remaining qualifications of the claim are accepted as visibly deferred; no N/A entry exists and no dummy passing test is treated as behavior evidence.

Baseline: independently compared historical input.json full sources to current files. spec_plan.rs is an exact byte match on both implementation/test sides. book.rs differs only in other tests: review start/record API migration and accepted/changes-requested/unfinished assertions, and claim lookup through fragments. The associated chapter test and its helpers are unchanged. Inspected and captured the relevant changed sections; they do not alter this claim's assertions or TODO rationale.

Execution: personally ran review start and review read and performed the baseline comparison; no behavioral test command was run. The coordinator separately reports 321 sage-meta tests and root cargo build passing; that is not reviewer execution evidence. All used current helper/source dependencies are captured. No source edits or additional tests are requested.
